sections.h2: Where do Woodford County, Kentucky owners take property tax questions?
sections.html:
Value questions go to the Property Valuation Administrator, and bill questions go to the sheriff. The valuation office sits in the courthouse at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, in Versailles, and the county directory lists it open Monday through Thursday until 4 and Friday until 5:30, starting at 8 each day. The sheriff's website lists 859-873-3119 and 859-873-3126 and offers bill search and online payment.

Assessment notices arrive each spring with the value assigned to the property. The sheriff mails tax bills in the last week of September and delinquent notices in February. The sheriff also warns that the office never sends threatening letters demanding property tax, so a demand from an unfamiliar "unit" with an 800 number is a scam to report, not pay.

sections.h2: What is Woodford County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Woodford is a Bluegrass county of 192 square miles in the Lexington metro area. Versailles is the seat and largest city, and Midway is the only other city. Fayette, Franklin, Scott, Jessamine, Mercer and Anderson counties ring it. The county was formed in 1788 from Fayette County, Virginia, and named for a Revolutionary War general, William Woodford. It was the last of the nine original Kentucky counties, and Scott and Franklin later took pieces of it.

The distillery known today for Woodford Reserve began as Labrot and Graham in 1812. Midway University, the Kentucky Castle and a youth outdoor program called the Life Adventure Center are here too, and a royal visitor stayed at Lane's End Farm in 2007. Schools include Woodford County High and Middle, and the elementary schools Huntertown, Northside, Southside and Simmons.

The survey figures for 2020 through 2024 describe an affluent market:

  • Middle owned home: $299,700.
  • Typical household income: $83,788, with 9.7 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Owners occupy 71.7 percent of households, and 40.7 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree.
  • Rent: $1,138 a month. Owner costs: $1,571 with a mortgage, $577 without.
  • Housing units: 11,917, with 95 new home permits in 2025.

sections.h2: How has the Woodford County population changed?
sections.html:
Growth has been steady. The county counted 14,434 people in 1970, 23,208 in 2000, 24,939 in 2010 and 26,871 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 27,883, up 3.8 percent. The median age in 2020 was 42.9, and 19.4 percent of residents were 65 or older. The census found 10,736 households and 11,487 housing units, 6.5 percent of them vacant, and 62.8 percent of residents live in urban areas. By the 2020 to 2024 survey, 22.5 percent are 65 or older and 9.4 percent identify as Hispanic or Latino.

Workers average 24 minutes to get to work. In 2023 the county had 618 employer establishments with 7,913 jobs and a payroll of $340.1 million, and retail sales hit $321.5 million in 2022.

sections.h2: What does the Woodford County tax year look like?
sections.html:
It follows the state calendar, summarized below from the Department of Revenue and KRS 134.015.

Yearly property tax steps for a Woodford County owner
WhenStep
January 1Assessment date, and the owner that day is taxed
First Monday in May, 13 daysTax roll open for public inspection
25 to 35 days after thatLocal board of assessment appeals meets
Through November 12 percent discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January5 percent penalty
After January 3110 percent penalty
April 15Unpaid bills go to the clerk with a lien

Source: Kentucky Department of Revenue, The Property Tax Calendar, and KRS 134.015.

A spring seller whose name was on the January 1 roll still owes that year's bill. The title company usually asks the sheriff for a current payoff before closing.

sections.h2: How does a Woodford County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
Begin with a conference at the PVA office, which the state requires. The office must explain how it reached your value and keep a written record of both sides' numbers. After that, file with the County Clerk by close of business on the workday following the end of the inspection period. If inspection runs May 3 to May 17, for example, the deadline is May 18.

  • Bring facts such as land and building details, insurance policies, construction costs and sale listings. Without evidence the appeal is denied.
  • A paid representative must be an attorney, accountant, broker, appraiser or similar professional with written authority from you.
  • You may record the hearing on audio, and the board must explain any change in writing.

Skipping the local board forfeits any later claim to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If bills print before your case ends and the final value beats your claim, a supplemental bill covers the difference.

sections.h2: Why are some Woodford County parcels valued differently?
sections.html:
Method depends on the property. Houses are valued by sales comparison, adjusted for items like a basement or garage. Barns and farm buildings use replacement cost less depreciation, and rentals use income. Farmland is assessed at agricultural value under Section 172A of the state constitution, which can sharply lower tax on open pasture. A buyer planning to subdivide should ask the PVA and the clerk what changes when use changes.

Every parcel may be revalued each year and must be inspected at least once in four years. If your number looks high, ask the PVA for the sales it relied on.

sections.h2: What does the Woodford County homestead exemption cover?
sections.html: Owners who reach 65, and the totally disabled, can have a fixed amount taken off the assessed value of their residence, once per household. File Form 62A350 with the PVA, and the exemption renews itself while the same applicant lives there. Disabled veterans with a service connected rating and holders of a permanent Social Security disability finding need not reapply. A buyer applies separately, and the PVA knows the current amount, which the state resets every two years.

sections.h2: What if a Woodford County bill is still open after April 15?
sections.html: The clerk records a lien and charges interest at 1 percent a month, plus commissions of 10 percent for the clerk and later 20 percent for the county attorney. The attorney mails a 30 day notice and a second notice before a sale held 90 to 135 days after the transfer. The lien under KRS 134.420 can last 11 years and stays with the parcel after a sale. Your payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and a private buyer of the certificate may add fees.

faqs.q: Who mails the Woodford County tax bill?
faqs.a: The sheriff mails it in the last week of September. The sheriff's website, which lists 859-873-3119 and 859-873-3126, has bill search and online payment.

faqs.q: How does a Woodford County owner dispute a value?
faqs.a: Meet the PVA first, then file with the County Clerk by the workday after the inspection period closes. The PVA office is at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, in Versailles.

faqs.q: How long does the Woodford County discount last?
faqs.a: Through November 1, at 2 percent. KRS 134.015 then sets face value to December 31, a 5 percent penalty in January and 10 percent afterward.

faqs.q: Does a Woodford County seller owe tax for the year of sale?
faqs.a: Possibly. The January 1 owner is taxed, and that name is on the bill. The contract and title company decide who pays at closing, so request a sheriff payoff first.

faqs.q: What should a Woodford County owner ask the PVA?
faqs.a: Ask which recent sales support your value and when the office last inspected the house. Those answers show whether an appeal is worth filing before the roll opens in May.
